decisions.reason: The terminology prohibition and confirmation of product-benefit alignment do not change the existing reference-based creative foundation or its relationship to the reference.
The source decision does not change the audience age range or Indian-market scope.
The source decision does not alter the source or presentation format of testimonial material.
The prohibited term and benefit alignment do not change the required call to action.
Prohibiting one Hindi term constrains product messaging but does not change the requirement that the script and preview be in Hindi.
The source decision does not modify hook directness or Indian-market alignment.
The message changes allowed product wording and benefit claims, not the required viral creative style.
Product-benefit messaging has no necessary effect on lip-sync accuracy or facial-expression requirements.
The source decision does not resolve or alter the live-action versus AI-generated production-method conflict.
The source decision does not change responsibility for sourcing the script, visuals, or voiceover.
The message does not change actor nationality or gender preferences.
The terminology and benefit decisions do not affect video count, duration, aspect ratios, or pilot expansion conditions.
